record.paper_title: Some open problems on the classical function space L1
record.original_question: Let 1 < s < p ≤ ∞. Must every bounded linear operator T: Lp → L1 factor through Ls, meaning that there exist bounded operators S: Lp → Ls and U: Ls → L1 with T = U ∘ S?

evidence.quote: Problem 11. ([77]) Let 1

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a standard non-atomic $\sigma$-finite measure space (for instance $[0,1]$ with Lebesgue measure) and, for $1\le r\le \infty$, let $L_r=L_r(\Omega,\mu)$ denote the usual Lebesgue space of (equivalence classes of) measurable scalar functions. Given Banach spaces $X,Y$, a bounded linear operator $T:X\to Y$ is said to factor through a Banach space $Z$ if there exist bounded linear operators $S:X\to Z$ and $U:Z\to Y$ such that $T=U\circ S$.

Fix real numbers $s$ and $p$ with $1<s<p\le \infty$. Determine whether every bounded linear operator $T:L_p\to L_1$ factors through $L_s$; that is, decide whether for every such $T$ there exist bounded linear operators $S:L_p\to L_s$ and $U:L_s\to L_1$ with $T=U\circ S$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every bounded operator $T:L_p\to L_1$ (with $1<s<p\le\infty$) factors through $L_s$ is a classical problem in the factorization theory of operators on $L_p$-spaces, related to work of Maurey, Rosenthal, and Pisier. Web searches surface the broader factorization framework (Pisier's "Factorization of Linear Operators and Geometry of Banach Spaces", Maurey's factorization theorems, and Pisier's 1986 paper on factorization through $L_{p\infty}$/$L_{p1}$), but no source was found that resolves this specific factorization question in the stated generality. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Factorization of Linear Operators and Geometry of Banach Spaces (Pisier, CBMS 60)
status_evidence.snippet: Monograph surveying factorization theorems for operators between L_p spaces, including Maurey-Rosenthal type results.
status_evidence.claim: The general framework of factoring operators between L_p spaces is treated, but the specific Lp→L1 through Ls problem is not stated as resolved.

status_evidence.title: Factorization of Operators Through L_{p∞} or L_{p1} and Non-Commutative Generalizations (Pisier, Math. Ann. 276, 1986)
status_evidence.snippet: Pisier studies factorization of operators through Lorentz spaces L_{p∞}, L_{p1} and noncommutative analogues.
status_evidence.claim: Provides related factorization results but does not settle whether every T:Lp→L1 factors through Ls for 1<s<p.

status_evidence.title: Type, cotype and K-convexity (Maurey)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses factorization through Lp, p>1, of operators with values in L1, including Rosenthal's theorem on q-summing adjoints.
status_evidence.claim: Classical partial results on factoring operators into L1 through L_p exist, but the general question for arbitrary T:Lp→L1 remains discussed as open.
